reviewer_type: AI-assisted claim-level source audit with independent read-only post-edit review; no human expert review is claimed.
title: The AI Box Scenario
scope: Claim-level traceability review of the revised article and matching dataset record. Focus: who devised and participated in the 2002 role-plays; reported outcomes; the distinction between terms agreed before the trials and Yudkowsky’s later proposed protocol; how the 2012 peer-reviewed Oracle-AI article relates to the role-play; and the limits of what human role-play establishes. This status does not establish that a real AI could persuade a gatekeeper, that containment is impossible or sufficient, scholarly consensus, exhaustive literature coverage, or expert review.
summary: Yudkowsky’s accessible author-hosted retrospective account says he played the AI in two 2002 text-chat trials, with Nathan Russell and David McFadzean as gatekeepers; the contemporary SL4 archive contains each gatekeeper’s report that he let the role-play AI out. Yudkowsky says the trials had no agreed rules beyond secrecy and a two-hour minimum and that his detailed public protocol was written afterward; he calls the results strictly anecdotal evidence. The Oxford repository verifies that Armstrong, Sandberg, and Bostrom later published a peer-reviewed Oracle-AI control analysis in 2012, whose Section 3 discusses Yudkowsky’s role-play; they were not participants in the trials. The article now distinguishes these sources and explicitly says no inference about actual AI capabilities is claimed. Independent read-only post-edit review found no material corrections. The five article Further Reading URLs match the dataset references, and date_verified is 2026-11-01.

sources.title: The AI-Box Experiment
sources.author: Eliezer S. Yudkowsky
sources.publication: Author-hosted retrospective account; page displays posting dates 4 September 2020 and 2 July 2021. It recounts role-plays conducted in 2002.
sources.access_level: The full accessible page and relevant linked text were retrieved and read; the original early-2000s Yudkowsky webpage was not independently accessed.
sources.exact_locations_read: Opening scenario; historical summary of the March and July 2002 trials; statements that only secrecy and a two-hour minimum were agreed beforehand; ‘Protocol for the AI,’ ‘Protocol for the Gatekeeper,’ ‘Protocol for Both Parties,’ and the note that the detailed suggested interpretation was written after the second test; ‘Suggestions,’ including the explicit statement that results are strictly anecdotal evidence.
sources.limitations: Retrospective first-person account, not a transcript of the private chats. Its detailed proposed protocol postdates the two trials. The author’s account and participants’ messages do not test an actual AI or establish general containment results.

sources.title: Re: The ‘AI Box’ experiment
sources.author: Nathan Russell
sources.publication: SL4 mailing-list archive, message dated 8 March 2002, 16:57:27 MST; message 3141 in the March 2002 archive.
sources.access_level: The full short message and its thread metadata were accessed and read.
sources.exact_locations_read: Message body: ‘I decided to let Eliezer out.’ Header date, sender, and thread metadata identify the contemporaneous report.
sources.limitations: The message records Russell’s reported outcome but not the private chat transcript, the persuasion content, or an independently controlled test. Participant and trial details are cross-checked against Yudkowsky’s retrospective account.

sources.title: AI-Box Experiment 2: Yudkowsky and McFadzean
sources.author: Eliezer S. Yudkowsky
sources.publication: SL4 mailing-list archive, message dated 4 July 2002, 12:05:44 MDT; message 4689 in the July 2002 archive.
sources.access_level: Full announcement and relevant quoted chat excerpt were accessed and read.
sources.exact_locations_read: Message body identifies David McFadzean as volunteer gatekeeper, records the agreed two-hour duration, $20 payment if the gatekeeper did not release the AI, private IRC setup, and secrecy agreement.
sources.limitations: This announcement records proposed terms and participant statements before the second trial, not the private trial transcript or evidence of how the conversation proceeded.

sources.title: Re: AI-Box Experiment 2: Yudkowsky and McFadzean
sources.author: David McFadzean
sources.publication: SL4 mailing-list archive, message dated 5 July 2002, 15:16:37 MDT; message 4721 in the July 2002 archive.
sources.access_level: The full short message and its thread metadata were accessed and read.
sources.exact_locations_read: Message body: ‘I let the transhuman AI out of the box.’ Header date and thread linkage identify it as the second gatekeeper’s report after the July 4 announcement.
sources.limitations: The message documents a participant’s reported outcome, not the private chat transcript, a controlled test, or any ability of a real AI.

sources.title: Thinking inside the box: using and controlling an Oracle AI
sources.author: Stuart Armstrong, Anders Sandberg, and Nick Bostrom
sources.publication: Minds and Machines 22(4), 2012, pp. 299–324; DOI 10.1007/s11023-012-9282-2. Oxford Research Archive lists the article as published and peer reviewed and provides an accepted manuscript.
sources.access_level: Oxford repository record and accessible accepted manuscript were read; relevant passages in the full manuscript were read. Publisher full text was not separately accessed.
sources.exact_locations_read: §3, ‘Human-level considerations,’ manuscript pp. 7–9, including its account of Yudkowsky’s role-play and social-engineering risk; §3.1 and §4 for discussion of limiting interaction and methods of control. Oxford record read for title, authors, publication status, peer-review status, journal citation, DOI, and accepted-manuscript link.
sources.limitations: The article is later analysis of Oracle-AI control, not a primary source for the 2002 events and not evidence that its authors participated in the role-play. The publisher version was not accessed.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Yudkowsky devised and role-played the AI in two 2002 text-chat trials, with Nathan Russell and David McFadzean as gatekeepers; each later reported that he let the role-play AI out.
claim_evidence.source_title: The AI-Box Experiment; contemporary SL4 messages 3141 and 4721
claim_evidence.exact_location: Yudkowsky page’s historical summary of the March and July 2002 trials; Russell’s 8 March 2002 message body; McFadzean’s 5 July 2002 message body.
claim_evidence.finding: The retrospective account identifies the participants and dates; contemporaneous mailing-list messages report the gatekeepers’ outcomes. The revised article describes these as human text-chat role-plays and reports, not as experiments on an actual AI.
claim_evidence.limitation: No private chat transcript was accessed; the outcomes are participants’ reports, not independently observed experimental data.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: restored a direct author account and contemporaneous outcome records, and explicitly distinguished role-play from tests of actual AI.

claim_evidence.material_claim: The 2002 trials had no agreed rules in advance beyond secrecy and a two-hour minimum; Yudkowsky’s detailed public protocol was proposed afterward.
claim_evidence.source_title: The AI-Box Experiment; AI-Box Experiment 2: Yudkowsky and McFadzean
claim_evidence.exact_location: Yudkowsky page, paragraph immediately before ‘Protocol for the AI’; July 2002 message 4689’s quoted arrangement for a two-hour trial and $20 handicap.
claim_evidence.finding: Yudkowsky explicitly says the earlier trials had only secrecy and a two-hour minimum agreed beforehand and that the suggested interpretation was created after the second trial. The second contemporaneous message independently records the planned duration and terms.
claim_evidence.limitation: The retrospective page reports the first test’s minimal terms; the July message directly records the second test’s arrangement. The full private negotiation or chat record was not accessed.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: stated the postdated-protocol distinction and retained no claim that every later rule governed the original tests.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Yudkowsky describes the role-play results as anecdotal; they do not establish that an actual AI could persuade a human, that containment is impossible, or that containment is sufficient.
claim_evidence.source_title: The AI-Box Experiment; Thinking inside the box: using and controlling an Oracle AI
claim_evidence.exact_location: Yudkowsky page, ‘Suggestions,’ final paragraph on anecdotal evidence; Armstrong et al., §3, ‘Human-level considerations,’ and §4 on control methods and limitations.
claim_evidence.finding: Yudkowsky explicitly calls results strictly anecdotal. The 2012 paper frames role-play as one illustration in a broader discussion of social engineering and Oracle-AI control; it does not experimentally demonstrate actual-AI persuasion. The revised article explicitly limits its inference.
claim_evidence.limitation: The 2012 paper is a scholarly analysis, not an empirical trial of AI capability; the publisher copy was not consulted.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: added the author's own anecdotal-evidence caveat and disclaimed inference about actual AI capabilities.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Armstrong, Sandberg, and Bostrom wrote a later peer-reviewed 2012 Oracle-AI control article that discusses Yudkowsky’s role-play; they did not participate in the 2002 trials.
claim_evidence.source_title: Thinking inside the box: using and controlling an Oracle AI
claim_evidence.exact_location: Oxford repository record for authors, 2012 publication, journal details, DOI, publication and peer-review status; accepted manuscript §3 on human-level considerations and Yudkowsky’s role-play.
claim_evidence.finding: The repository metadata and manuscript support the later analysis and authorship. The article now explicitly separates these researchers from the 2002 participants and describes the source as a peer-reviewed article rather than only a manuscript.
claim_evidence.limitation: The accepted manuscript rather than publisher full text was read; the paper’s later analysis does not independently prove the role-play outcomes.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: corrected the publication description and attribution, and cited the Oxford record with accepted-manuscript access.

unresolved: The original early-2000s Yudkowsky webpage was not independently retrieved; the currently accessible author page is retrospective, while contemporary mailing-list messages corroborate the reported events.
Private chat transcripts were not accessed, so the content and process of persuasion remain unknown.
The role-play does not support empirical conclusions about actual AI or superintelligent-system capability.
post_edit_review: Independent read-only review found no material corrections; it checked history, protocol timing, participants, reported outcomes, 2012 article attribution, and article/dataset URL alignment.
